title: Docs + terminal cross-surface isolation, scale-recall & end-to-end verification (runs last)
priority_note: Terminal story: owns the epic-wide isolation proof, the at-scale recall check, and the docs, so no earlier story is blocked mid-loop on cross-surface concerns. Mirrors epic_27's US-27.17.

background.reference: GitHub issue #307; mirrors epic_27's terminal verification story (US-27.17). Enhanced-review round 1 applied: cross-SUBJECT isolation must be proven on the API too (not just the context), the subject-scoped recall must be verified at scale (HNSW under-fill risk), and there is no LiveView surface (loopctl is agent-native).
background.includes: Every prior story asserts its own slice; this story proves the pillar end-to-end across context/API/MCP, proves cross-tenant AND cross-subject isolation everywhere, verifies subject-scoped recall at prod-like scale, and writes the memory-vs-knowledge documentation. Depends on every leaf story and runs DEAD LAST.

story.i_want_to: run one end-to-end pass that writes and recalls memory through every surface (context, API, MCP), proves cross-tenant/cross-subject isolation everywhere, and proves subject-scoped recall holds at scale, plus document the memory-vs-knowledge boundary
story.so_that: the agent-memory pillar ships proven and understandable, not just unit-green

rationale: Scope isolation (tenant AND subject) is the security property of the whole subsystem, and asserting it once per layer is not the same as asserting it holds across the full write->embed->recall path — especially since subject isolation is application-level (BYPASSRLS heavy-read) and can silently under-fill at scale. A single terminal verification (the epic_27 model) plus authoritative docs turns a set of merged stories into a trustworthy, teachable feature.

acceptance_criteria.description: docs/agent-memory.md is written: subsystem architecture, the two tiers (session vs long-term) and session TTL/pruning, the scope model (subject_id derivation + the BYPASSRLS heavy-read structural guard), and an explicit 'when to use memory vs knowledge (vs the future context retriever)' section. It absorbs any durable content the removed docs/cole-medin-self-evolving-wiki.md carried (now KB hub fb9abd73). It states loopctl is agent-native (no web UI) and that operator oversight is the superadmin API path.
README.md (feature + memory_* tool list), CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (agent guidance: pick memory_* vs knowledge_*), and CHANGELOG.md are updated; the memory endpoints render at /swaggerui.

An end-to-end integration test writes a memory via the API, drains embedding, then recalls it via BOTH Loopctl.Memory and the API, asserting the same memory is reachable through each with the pinned result shape — one coherent path.

A cross-surface isolation suite proves a memory written under (tenant T, subject A) is NOT retrievable as tenant U, NOR as subject B of T, through the context AND the API AND (where testable) the MCP tool — closing both the cross-tenant and cross-subject leak surfaces epic-wide.

A @tag :scale recall test seeds a subject with N memories among a much larger multi-subject corpus (reuse US-27.1 ANALYZE-at-scale seeding) and asserts the subject reliably recalls its own top-k — proving the subject filter did not get starved by HNSW under-fill (US-28.2 AC-28.2.3). Excluded from mix precommit; executed here.

The docs record a PII/secret stance: memory text is embedded by a third-party (per-tenant BYO) provider, so memory content leaves the tenant boundary to the embedding API; the docs state what should NOT be stored as memory and note the write path is rate-limited + per-scope capped.

A documented seam note records where #308 (auto-promotion) and mkreyman/claude-config#85 (skills consumer) hook in (source=:promoted, supersede/2, session_history/2, which memory_* tools the skills call). No implementation of those here — only the verified extension points.

test_cases.name: End-to-end write(API) then recall(context + API) for one memory
preconditions: embedding client stubbed via Mox to deterministic vectors
steps: Loopctl.Memory.recall(scope, %{query: ...}) and POST /api/v1/memory/recall with the same query
expected_results: both recalls return the same memory id with a score in the pinned %{results, meta} shape
the API and context results agree

test_cases.name: Cross-tenant and cross-subject isolation holds on context and API
preconditions: {_, key_tb} = fixture(:api_key, tenant: tenant_t, role: :agent)  # subject B of T
m = fixture(:memory, tenant: tenant_t, subject_id: "A", text: "T/A secret"); drain embedding
steps: recall/list/forget m as key_u via the API
recall/list/forget m as key_tb (subject B) via the API
recall/list/forget m as (tenant_t, subject B) via Loopctl.Memory
expected_results: m is never returned or mutated on any surface, cross-tenant or cross-subject

test_cases.name: Subject-scoped recall survives at scale (no HNSW under-fill)
preconditions: seed a large multi-subject corpus (>= prod floor) with subject A holding N distinctive memories, ANALYZEd (US-27.1 helper)
steps: recall as subject A for a query matching A's memories
expected_results: A's top-k own memories are returned (not starved by other subjects dominating the ANN pool)

technical_notes: Model on epic_27's US-27.17 terminal-verification pattern: depends on all leaves, runs last, owns the @tag :scale checks excluded from mix precommit.

docs/agent-memory.md is authoritative for the three-layer mental model (knowledge / memory / context-retriever) the Cole Medin comparison surfaced — keep it short and decision-oriented; state loopctl is agent-native (no web UI).
There is NO LiveView/inspector surface (removed — loopctl has no human web auth); operator oversight is the superadmin API path in US-28.3 AC-28.3.4.
Do NOT implement #308 or claude-config#85 here; only assert and document the seams they rely on.
Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/2; reuse the deterministic Mox embedding stub from US-28.2 and the ScaleSeed helper from US-27.1.
